subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm: fix two allocator races with zonelist and cpuset updates

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author responded to feedback that the patch's cpuset_nodemask_valid_mems_allowed() function may erroneously drop a nodemask on a race condition, explaining that the loop in this function ensures nodemask and mems_allowed are stable when compared, and that the cookie-check in check_retry_cpuset() runs after the nodemask would already have been dropped.
reviews.raw_body:
No I don't think so. We're checking different things.

The loop here makes sure nodemask and mems_allowed are stable when
compared so we don't erroneously drop the nodemask on a race.

The cookie-check in check_retry_cpuset() determines whether the entire
allocation should restart.  It runs after the nodemask would already
have been dropped, so it can't catch this race.

~Gregory

2026-10-15.patch_summary: This patch addresses two races in the Linux kernel's memory allocator that can occur when updating zonelists and cpusets concurrently. The first issue arises from a retry mechanism for zonelist updates, which can lead to inconsistent views of state between CPUs. The second problem involves a comparison between a mempolicy nodemask and the current mems_allowed without considering the sequence number, resulting in spurious empty intersections and unnecessary policy relaxations. The patches fix these issues by introducing additional checks and using the correct sequence numbers for updates. These changes aim to prevent allocation failures and ensure that memory policies are correctly enforced.
